name: Pelatiah and the princes at the east gate
charge: Devising mischief and giving wicked counsel in the city
summary: In vision Ezekiel saw twenty-five men at the east gate of the temple, princes of the people, Jaazaniah and Pelatiah among them, who said, it is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh. He was told to prophesy against them.
offense: At the east gate in Ezekiel's vision stood twenty-five men, including Pelatiah, who devised mischief and gave wicked counsel. Their saying that the city was the cauldron and they the flesh was answered by the Lord, who knew the things that came into their minds. They had multiplied the slain and filled the streets with them. God reversed their image: the slain were the flesh within the city, while the counselors themselves would be brought out. Their confidence could not shelter the men responsible for bloodshed and corrupt counsel.
judgment: The Lord announced that He would bring the sword they feared and judge them at the border of Israel. As Ezekiel prophesied in the vision, Pelatiah died. The prophet fell upon his face and cried out, fearing a full end of the remnant. God answered with a word concerning the scattered people. Though removed far away, He would be a little sanctuary to them and would gather them again. He promised one heart and a new spirit, that they might walk in His statutes. The fall of a corrupt counselor was thus followed by assurance that restoration would rest upon God's work and renewed obedience, not upon Jerusalem's boast.
offenseFull: At the east gate in Ezekiel's vision stood twenty-five men, including Pelatiah, who devised mischief and gave wicked counsel. Their saying that the city was the cauldron and they the flesh was answered by the Lord, who knew the things that came into their minds.

They had multiplied the slain and filled the streets with them. God reversed their image: the slain were the flesh within the city, while the counselors themselves would be brought out. Their confidence could not shelter the men responsible for bloodshed and corrupt counsel.
judgmentFull: The Lord announced that He would bring the sword they feared and judge them at the border of Israel. As Ezekiel prophesied in the vision, Pelatiah died. The prophet fell upon his face and cried out, fearing a full end of the remnant.

God answered with a word concerning the scattered people. Though removed far away, He would be a little sanctuary to them and would gather them again. He promised one heart and a new spirit, that they might walk in His statutes. The fall of a corrupt counselor was thus followed by assurance that restoration would rest upon God's work and renewed obedience, not upon Jerusalem's boast.

verses.text: Moreover the spirit lifted me up, and brought me unto the east gate of the Lord’s house, which looketh eastward: and behold at the door of the gate five and twenty men; among whom I saw Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people.
Then said he unto me, Son of man, these are the men that devise mischief, and give wicked counsel in this city:
Which say, It is not near; let us build houses: this city is the caldron, and we be the flesh.
Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy, O son of man.
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Your slain whom ye have laid in the midst of it, they are the flesh, and this city is the caldron: but I will bring you forth out of the midst of it.
Ye have feared the sword; and I will bring a sword upon you, saith the Lord God.
And I will bring you out of the midst thereof, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you.
Ye shall fall by the sword; I will judge you in the border of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
This city shall not be your caldron, neither shall ye be the flesh in the midst thereof; but I will judge you in the border of Israel:
And ye shall know that I am the Lord: for ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen that are round about you.

And it came to pass, when I prophesied, that Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. Then fell I down upon my face, and cried with a loud voice, and said, Ah Lord God! wilt thou make a full end of the remnant of Israel?
Her princes in the midst thereof are like wolves ravening the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls, to get dishonest gain.
Hear this, I pray you, ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment, and pervert all equity.
They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.

The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? none evil can come upon us.

entries.commentary: The spirit lifted Ezekiel up and brought him to the east gate of the Lord's house, where he saw five and twenty men, among whom were Jaazaniah the son of Azur and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people; remember the name Pelatiah. These are the men that devise mischief and give wicked counsel in the city, telling the people it is not near, let us build houses, this city is the cauldron and we are the flesh. Babylon had already carried away the northern kingdom and some of our people were already in captivity, yet the counsel was that Jerusalem, the iron pot, would protect them, giving the people a false sense of security. The Most High tells Ezekiel to prophesy against these twenty-five wicked men.

The spirit of the Most High fell upon Ezekiel and told him to say that He knows the things that come into their minds, every one of them. They had multiplied their slain in the city and filled the streets with the dead, for the land was full of blood and violence. The dead they laid in the midst of the city are the flesh, and the city is the cauldron, but the Most High will bring them forth out of the midst of it. Because they feared the sword, He will bring a sword upon them, meaning He will bring the nations against Jerusalem.

The Most High will deliver them into the hands of strangers, the nations, and execute judgments among them so that they fall by the sword in the border of Israel and know that He is the Lord. This city will not be their cauldron, neither will they be the flesh in the midst of it; He will judge them in the border of Israel. We get judged because we do not keep the Most High's laws, the same then as today; they had not walked in His statutes but had done after the manners of the heathen around about them. -

While Ezekiel was prophesying, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died, one of the wicked men that had given wicked counsel, put to death by the Most High. Ezekiel fell upon his face and cried with a loud voice, asking if the Most High would make a full end of the remnant of Israel.

The word of the Lord came again, calling them Ezekiel's brethren, the men of his kindred and the house of Israel, unto whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem had said, get you far from the Lord, this land is given to us in possession. Although the Most High has cast them far off among the heathen and scattered them among the countries, He will yet be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they come. Everywhere we are scattered the little sanctuaries are a comfort, just like the schools IUIC is setting up in all our scattered lands, where you come and learn the word of God.

The Most High will gather them from the people and assemble them out of the countries where they were scattered and give them the land of Israel, and they shall take away all its detestable things and abominations. He will give them one heart and put a new spirit within them, putting all of us on one accord with the word of God. He will take the stony heart, the rebellious mind that rebels against His laws, out of their flesh and give them a heart of flesh, a future prophecy of what will happen, that they may walk in His statutes and be His people. But as for those whose heart walks after their detestable things, the wicked Israelites who will not do this, He will recompense their way upon their own heads; there is a big payback when you will not keep His laws.

The cherubims lifted up their wings and the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above. The glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain on the east side, then the spirit took Ezekiel up in a vision by the spirit of God into Chaldea, to them of the captivity. The vision went up from Ezekiel, and he spoke unto the captives in Babylon all the things the Most High had showed him. -

The word of the Most High comes to Ezekiel to judge the bloody city, Jerusalem, and show her all her abominations. She has shed blood in her midst and made idols against herself to defile herself, causing her days to draw near. Because of her idolatry and wickedness, once judgment comes He makes her a reproach unto the heathen and a mocking to all countries, both near and far.

The princes of Israel used their power to shed blood, set light by father and mother, dealt by oppression with the stranger, and vexed the fatherless and the widow. They despised His holy things, profaned His sabbaths, carried tales to shed blood, ate upon the mountains, and committed lewdness in her midst. They broke all manner of the immoral laws of [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18), committing abomination with a neighbor's wife, defiling a daughter-in-law, and humbling a sister, doing the doings of the other nations. They took gifts to shed blood, being put on the take and paid off to shed a man's blood, took usury and increase, and greedily gained by extortion, and have forgotten Him; these are wicked leaders.

The Most High smites His hand at their dishonest gain and at the blood shed in their midst, asking whether their heart can endure or their hands be strong in the day He deals with them. He will scatter them among the heathen, disperse them in the countries, and consume their filthiness out of them, and they shall know that He is the Lord when they take their inheritance in the sight of the heathen.

The house of Israel is become dross to Him, all brass, tin, iron, and lead, the dross of silver in the midst of the furnace. He will gather them into the midst of Jerusalem as men gather metal into the furnace, and blow the fire of His wrath upon them. They shall be melted in the midst of the furnace as silver is melted, and shall know that He is the Lord who poured out His fury upon them.

The land is not cleansed nor rained upon, and there is a conspiracy of her prophets in her midst, like a roaring lion ravening the prey, devouring souls and making many widows; the leaders of Israel are very corrupt. Her priests violated His law and profaned His holy things, putting no difference between the holy and the profane or the clean and the unclean and hiding their eyes from His sabbaths, just like today where our people put no difference between anything, and it is called Christianity. Her princes are like wolves ravening the prey to shed blood and destroy souls for dishonest gain, and her prophets daub them with untempered mortar, seeing vanity and divining lies, saying thus saith the Lord God when He has not spoken. The people used oppression, exercised robbery, and vexed the poor and needy and the stranger wrongfully, showing the same oppression, robbery, and extortion by the leadership. He sought for a man to make up the hedge and stand in the gap before Him so He would not destroy the land, but He found none, so He poured out His indignation and consumed them with the fire of His wrath. -

Hear, I pray you, O heads of Jacob, and ye princes of the house of Israel; Is it not for you to know judgment? Who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones; who also eat the flesh of my people. Then shall they cry unto the Lord, but he will not hear them: he will even hide his face from them at that time, as they have behaved themselves ill in their doings.

Thus saith the Lord concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and he that putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him. Night shall be unto you, that ye shall not have a vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine. Then shall the seers be ashamed, and the diviners confounded, for there is no answer of God. But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the Lord, and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin.

Ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment, and pervert all equity; they build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity. The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? none evil can come upon us. Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of the forest.

lawsResolved.text: Irresponsible civil leaders are they who are either blind, ignorant, lazy, greedy, self-centered, drunkards, or act for their own gain.

Government officers are to execute judgment and righteousness, and deliver the spoiled out of the hand of the oppressor; they are to do no wrong, do no violence to the stranger, the fatherless, nor the widow, neither shed innocent blood in the land.
If a ruler hearken to lies, all his aides and ministers become wicked.
Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
We are not to learn or follow the ways, customs or abominations of the heathen or of any ungodly nation.
